title: Component Architecture Candidates
purpose: Organize source-influenced reusable presentation relationships that may become typed Kotlin Blueprint contracts after cross-platform pressure, without promoting Android source or Screen Lens projections into portable semantic authority.

sourceSnapshots.role: Canonical VexLife component / experience Blueprint meaning
Android/Kotlin/Compose realization and architectural pressure evidence
Accepted Kotlin semantic/Blueprint authoring, VexWeb relational grammar and deterministic browser artifact generation
Component Library architecture and Screen Lens projection machinery

candidates.label: Identity-addressed presentation tree
candidates.question: How can every nested presentation node remain stably addressable across source nesting, runtime realization, tests and Screen Lens without making visual position its identity?
portableRelationships: stable semantic ref survives renderer/framework changes
child identity derives beneath an explicit semantic parent
containment remains inspectable independently of rendered object identity
target source can project the same identity tree back to Screen Lens
obligations: identity must not depend on list index or transient render position
nested custom presentation must not silently lose parent continuity
duplicate identities fail closed
targetPressure: SwiftUI accessibilityIdentifier or equivalent projection hook

sourceEvidence.why: Accepted commonMain Kotlin Blueprint already exposes compiler-visible stable element handles and parent relationships independently of renderer/runtime state.
Nested source topology forms stable element paths and parent relationships.
Custom Compose presentation inherits semantic parent identity and fails closed outside a parent scope.
Platform modifier chains attach already-owned semantic identity without becoming another identity system.
Canonical VexLife components already distinguish stable component/instance/slot identities.

candidates.note: Strong first Kotlin Blueprint root law: identity before renderer.

candidates.label: Semantic control binding
candidates.question: How can a visible control bind to stable action meaning while each platform remains free to choose the appropriate native interaction form?
portableRelationships: control identity is separate from semantic action identity
interaction form may vary without redefining the action
availability/exposure can be projected separately from action meaning
obligations: one stable semantic action/ref is addressable independently of native callback syntax
platform adapter must preserve capability/permission obligations when present
native event wiring cannot become canonical meaning
targetPressure: voice or model-tool expression of the same action

sourceEvidence.why: Typed intent/action identity is separate from native Compose cells.
VexLife already allows button, native control, menu, vessel, voice and model-tool forms to express stable semantic meaning.
Presentation may change form without becoming semantic truth owner.
VexLife-Prod PR #506 pressure maps current typed Quick Actions relationships to native SwiftUI source while preserving exact source refs and binding meaning in a reverse-projection manifest.

candidates.note: The portable contract should say what action/control relationship exists, not which widget class handles it.

candidates.label: Typed containment and slots
candidates.question: How can source visually communicate what fits inside what while preserving explicit parent/child/slot relationships for target generation and Screen Lens?
portableRelationships: parent owns admitted child/slot topology
source nesting and normalized containment graph agree
layout form and semantic ownership remain distinct
obligations: target adapter preserves child ownership/topology
invalid child placement fails before generation where contract can know it
mustNotOwn: feature state merely because it contains feature presentation

sourceEvidence.why: Current Product composition is readable as nested Kotlin handles whose stable parent/child structure is independent of renderer implementation.
Nested DSL mirrors the intended containment tree and registry can recover parent/children.
Canonical components already expose stable slot relationships independent of rendering technology.

candidates.note: This is the composable readability Victor is pointing at: code nesting should carry relationship meaning, not just syntax.

candidates.label: Swappable region
candidates.question: How can one stable region switch among direct child expressions without creating app-navigation depth or duplicating ownership?
portableRelationships: one stable container owns a selected direct child
selection is local presentation, not app navigation
default child is explicit
obligations: selected child must belong directly to the region
switching does not fabricate screen navigation history
targetPressure: SwiftUI target generation HELD until current Product owns one compiler-visible local selection/default-child relationship
Current VexLife-Prod behavior is split across typed VexWeb structure and browser-local state.view

sourceEvidence.why: Gallery proves peer expressions under one stable region via swapTo rather than screen navigation.
Registry validates direct-child and same-scope SwapTo relationships.

Current typed presentation source establishes one local content container with Conversation/Settings children and a local-interaction switch control, but does not encode the full selected/default-child contract.
Current browser runtime owns the missing local selection facts: default conversation, settings/conversation toggle, mutually exclusive visibility, and no app-navigation depth.

candidates.note: Cross-Product pressure now exposes a source-contract gap: Android has typed Swappable/SwapTo; current VexLife-Prod has equivalent lived local presentation behavior, but default/selected-child truth is split between VexWeb structure and browser JS. Do not let a SwiftUI adapter reconstruct that architecture from runtime strings. Form or bind the rightful typed Product contract first.

candidates.label: Modal presentation contract
candidates.question: How can modal meaning remain stable while a target chooses alert, sheet, popover or another native modality?
portableRelationships: modal identity is separate from native modality
open/close/dismiss remain typed presentation relationships
modal children remain owned by the modal scope
obligations: target must report how modality was realized
platform-native dismissal maps to modal dismissal rather than fabricating another control activation
mustNotOwn: feature semantic state unless explicitly bound

sourceEvidence.why: One semantic/presentation identity is wrapped by distinct Android-native modal realizations.
Gallery carries both modal realization patterns under the same local presentation ownership rules.

candidates.label: Stable repeated-item collection
candidates.question: How can runtime-data rows retain stable semantic identity through insert/reorder/visibility changes without making visual index canonical?
portableRelationships: collection has one stable ref
each runtime item supplies stable identity
visual position is not item identity
visible-item set may be projected without owning item meaning
obligations: duplicate/blank item refs fail closed
target adapter preserves stable-key semantics
optional header/empty content cannot collide with item identity
targetPressure: VexLife-Prod ConversationTimeline: durable messageRef/eventRef identity + ordinary browser list rebuild
SwiftUI ForEach/List keyed by feature-owned stable item identity
VexLife-Prod #506 exact SwiftUI reference: messageRef -> Identifiable.id / ForEach / View.id
SwiftUI requested-visible / visible-item / scroll-lock relationships remain HELD pending target API proof

sourceEvidence.why: Several materially different Android consumers earned stable repeated-item mechanics independent of feature meaning.
Current Product Blueprint already identifies ConversationTimeline as a collection without making runtime messages static Blueprint elements.
Durable Conversation rows already carry feature-owned stable identity and chronology coordinates independently of visual list position.

Browser realization currently rebuilds ordinary timeline nodes with replaceChildren while separately preserving the mounted live-stream node, exposing real pressure for reusable stable repeated-item mechanics.

VexLife-Prod PR #506 maps the current ConversationTimeline collection + durable messageRef/eventRef/sequence coordinates into SwiftUI stable item identity while explicitly holding unproved viewport mechanics.

candidates.note: Cross-platform pressure is now real: Android has VexStableLazyColumn; current VexLife-Prod has stable Conversation message identity but ordinary browser renders rebuild the timeline while live streaming requires mounted-node preservation. A portable contract should own stable repeated-item mechanics only, leaving message meaning/order/store with Conversation.

candidates.label: Anchored transient overlay
candidates.question: How can transient context remain aimed at one semantic target while placement adapts to available window geometry?
portableRelationships: overlay names one semantic anchor
preferred placement order is explicit
safe-boundary fallback is target realization mechanics
overlay meaning remains caller-owned
obligations: target must keep target-relative relationship inspectable
placement adaptation must not change the semantic anchor
mustNotOwn: blocking semantics unless declared by caller

sourceEvidence.why: Android separates target-relative overlay relationship from platform geometry resolution and caller-owned meaning.

candidates.label: Local navigation trail
candidates.question: How can layered exploration inside one Screen own local depth/back without contaminating app-level navigation history?
portableRelationships: local trail root/current/path are scoped beneath one Screen
push/back mutate local depth
Back at local root yields to the outer navigation owner
direction follows the same path mutation
obligations: must remain distinct from app Screen navigation
duplicate current destination does not create depth
target adapter must preserve outer-back fallthrough
mustNotOwn: durable process restoration unless separately earned
targetPressure: SwiftUI NavigationStack scoped inside a surface

sourceEvidence.why: Android makes local depth/back a separate owner from AppNavigationState.

candidates.label: Context Dock
candidates.question: How can a host expose multiple feature-owned contextual projections with selection and reveal depth without absorbing their semantic ownership?
portableRelationships: each page has stable identity independent of visual pager index
horizontal axis selects context
vertical axis changes reveal depth
feature keeps page state/actions/meaning
host owns only presentation mechanics
obligations: page reordering/presence change preserves selected identity where possible
empty page set renders no fabricated context
target adapter keeps selection identity separate from index

sourceEvidence.why: Two independent presentation axes are reusable while page semantics stay with contributing features.

candidates.note: Excellent candidate for testing whether the Kotlin Blueprint can describe richer composable structure without carrying Compose implementation details.

candidates.label: Frame / seam / region layout
candidates.question: How can desktop/web-scale regions, dividers and overlays be authored as relationships rather than pixel positions or target-specific layout code?
portableRelationships: frame owns bounded regions
seam divides one axis with authored allocation
region edges bind to frame edges or seams
overlay layer is separate from frame geometry
obligations: layout graph fails closed on invalid seam/region references
target geometry may vary while relational bounds stay stable

sourceEvidence.why: Accepted sealed Kotlin relationship source owns Frame/Seam/Region spatial meaning and validation without encoding HTML/CSS.
Accepted Kotlin DSL forms the existing relationship objects and remains explicitly separate from renderer/generator meaning.
Accepted deterministic target adapter maps validated relationship objects to browser-native artifacts and a semantic manifest that preserves source relationships.
Screen Lens consumes/project this source-authored spatial grammar without becoming its authority.

candidates.note: This likely becomes more important for Chromebook/Linux/desktop than for phone-first UI.

candidates.label: Adaptive Action Vessel
candidates.question: How can one stable action/status vessel adapt between floating and docked native forms while preserving the same slots, actions and identity?
portableRelationships: stable component identity
trigger/menu/status slots remain addressable
resize affordances are explicit slots
platform chooses floating/docked/native manifestation
obligations: slot/action identities remain stable across platform form
platform adaptation does not invent new semantic action identities
mustNotOwn: platform window-manager policy beyond declared constraints
targetPressure: Kotlin Blueprint -> target adapter -> native source -> target semantic manifest / Screen Lens

sourceEvidence.why: VexLife already owns this as a platform-adaptive component with stable trigger/menu/status/resize slots.
Canonical VexLife Blueprint already distinguishes target bindings without collapsing them into one implementation.

candidates.note: Canonical predecessor Action Vessel remains a strong convergence target, but the first current-source SwiftUI pressure uses VexLife-Prod Quick Actions. Keep those identities distinct until cross-Product evidence earns convergence.

candidates.label: Adaptive action group
candidates.question: How can one stable action group and its trigger become a native Menu, floating cluster, toolbar group or other platform-appropriate presentation without losing action identity or source bindings?
portableRelationships: group identity is distinct from trigger identity
action children retain stable identities and bindings
target-native structure may differ from source containment
target manifest explicitly records each source node's target role and binding realization
obligations: target adaptation preserves source refs and binding targets
native trigger mechanics remain observable rather than silently replacing the source relationship
human words remain localization-owned rather than generator-owned
mustNotOwn: claim that every platform must use the same native container
targetPressure: SwiftUI Menu + Menu label + Menu actions

sourceEvidence.why: Current Product source owns one stable Quick Actions collection, one separate trigger and stable child identities.
Current accepted manifestation source binds the same identities to LocalInteraction, PresentationAction and ExternalNavigation relationships.
VexLife-Prod PR #506 pressure maps current typed Quick Actions relationships to native SwiftUI source while preserving exact source refs and binding meaning in a reverse-projection manifest.

candidates.note: First iOS pressure shows source collection+trigger can lawfully realize as SwiftUI Menu+label. This is source-influenced evidence, not portable acceptance.
